## Council question

May players record public deals despite the Atreides-only notes rule?

## Why this needs a ruling

Quickstart v0.8 limits written notes to Atreides and Treachery cards, but later says nonstandard deals are generally written down.

## Answer needed

Confirm whether recording public agreements is an exception, who may keep the record, and whether private non-card notes are permitted.

## Provisional drafting approach

Separate a shared record of public agreements from private information tracking if that is the intended distinction.

This is a research question, not an adopted ruling or a claim that Norbert has answered it. No answer has been supplied yet. Keep the affected rules provisional until Norbert or the council confirms them.

## Sources

Quickstart v0.8, Common Rules Clarifications and deal etiquette.

Part of #1831. Record the confirmed answer, its date and a worked example here before closing. Norbert will share this link with the council; this ticket does not send them a message.

comments.body:
Confirmed by Norbert on 14 October 2026:

> No player may write down notes for the purposes of remembering cards seen, spice transferred, etc. or other game related things that happen during play.
>
> Players may if the table agrees, write down binding deals so their wording will not be forgotten.
>
> Player may send each other written messages, but once read, must be removed/erased from play.

**Rule:**
- No notes to remember what happened in play: cards seen, spice transferred or any other game event.
- Binding deals may be written down when the table agrees, so their wording is not forgotten.
- Players may pass written messages, but a message must be removed or erased once it has been read.

**Worked example:** Fremen and Guild agree a binding deal: Guild ships Fremen troops for free this turn, and Fremen won't attack Tuek's Sietch. The table agrees, so the deal is written down to keep its exact wording. Guild then passes Fremen a note that says "I hold a Lasgun". Fremen reads it and it is destroyed. Fremen may not write down "Guild has a Lasgun", and Guild may not keep a list of the spice it has paid out.

Closing as answered. The Dream Rulebook draft's notes and deal-etiquette text still needs updating to match; that's a manuscript edit on #1831.

Atreides exception, confirmed by Norbert on 14 October 2026 (dictated; tidied here):

> Yes, the Atreides is allowed to keep written notes on game events that have occurred, including which Treachery cards they see during bidding or Treachery cards they've seen people play. Actually the Atreides is only allowed to keep notes about Treachery cards, nothing else: not things that people have said or spice transferred, only about Treachery cards and their whereabouts.

**Rule:** Atreides is the only exception to the no-notes rule. Atreides may write down Treachery cards and where they are: cards seen during bidding, cards seen played, and who holds or discarded which card. Atreides may not note anything else: not what people said, not spice transferred, not other game events.

**Worked example:** during bidding, Atreides sees that the card up for bid is a Lasgun and Harkonnen buys it. Atreides writes "Harkonnen: Lasgun". When Harkonnen later plays the Lasgun in battle, Atreides updates the note to "Lasgun: discarded". Atreides may not write "Harkonnen paid 4 spice" or "Fremen promised to stay out of Carthag".

This settles the open point on #2214. The Atreides sheet should state this exception.
